cross_module_name_conflicts.name: scratch
cross_module_name_conflicts.finding: Same construction call (scratch_model(cfg, 'rotated_discrete', 7717)) but different fresh seeds because the offset is relative to the module's model seed: SO2 5000 -> 12717, SO4 7000 -> 14717. SO4's seed is registered in SO4_B2_RETEST_PLAN.md:54/69-70, and SO2/SO4 use different worlds, so the arms are never paired. Also both use the slow rotated_discrete class for scratch while the trained arm is rotated_discrete_fast (documented in SO2's scratch_kind, ~1e-7 agreement). Not a mislabel.

cross_module_name_conflicts.name: scratch
cross_module_name_conflicts.finding: Name overlap only: V1's 'scratch' is a per-task NumPy ScratchResidualMLP (no shared library), the E/G5/SO line's scratch is a fresh operator library adapted on support. Different research lines and estimands; no report compares them. Not flagged as (c).

cross_module_name_conflicts.name: SHAM (outside the grep; noted for completeness)
cross_module_name_conflicts.finding: H50/H51/H53 SHAM = same trained start, same optimizer/data, no structure (the review-71 sham rule; copy.deepcopy(base) at h50:162 / h51:258). J1's SHAM is a different construction (per-round route reassignment, per the J1 census). Different lines with differently-registered shams; not a scratch/fresh mislabel, but the name does not denote one construction repository-wide.

list_differences: None in module identity: 26 modules match the site grep; removing audit_e6b_search_savings.py and audit_e9_partial_coverage.py (which import arm_provenance) leaves exactly the 24 listed.

Wording nuance: FOLLOWUP says '2 of them use arm_provenance (audit_e6_corpus.py, audit_e6b_search_savings.py)'. audit_e6_corpus.py does not match the site grep at all, so the 26 = 24 + e6b + e9. And e9 only imports describe_arm without calling it, so it is not actually checked either.

The grep includes 13 hits in scratch_difficulty.py that are references to the CONFIG FIELD `config.scratch_model` (the V1 NumPy scratch control's dataclass), not the `scratch_model()` function in audit_e1_export.py. Plus imports, docstrings, a comment and protocol strings. Only 13 of the 64 matching lines are actual arm constructions or definitions (see counts).
e5_reporting_check: The module's reporting STILL calls the arm scratch. (1) Docstring line 8-10: 'S (scratch)'. (2) Local variable `scratch_lib` at line 254. (3) Output keys are the bare 'S' in geomean_nmse, cost and oracle_gap for every world/setting, and the printed summary line 300 prints 'S ...' beside OPT. (4) decisions: the D6 gate (lines 311-314) computes log(S) - log(O) as the scratch-eligibility margin and labels failure 'UNINTERPRETABLE (oracle gate failed)', i.e. it treats S as the scratch reference. (5) The frozen plan E5_SYNTHESIZER_PLAN.md:39 defines S as 'fresh library and route'. The committed report reports/e5_synthesizer.json contains no 'scratch' string (keys are only 'S'), and neither the module nor the report carries any pointer to the PREDICTIONS.md:6377 correction. So the label is corrected only in PREDICTIONS.md / AGENTS.md / EXPORT_BRANCH_SESSION_REPORT.md, not in the module's reporting. Side observation: EXPORT_BRANCH_SESSION_REPORT.md:168 quotes the corrected world-0 D=6 gate margin as '2.02 -> 1.74', while PREDICTIONS.md:6396-6398 gives ~1.79 (2.02 - 0.23); the two documents disagree by 0.05.
